note: Machine-readable inventory of everything this fork adds on top of upstream. Drives `bun run fork:verify` (run after every sync to prove nothing was silently dropped) and `bun run sync:check` (detect when upstream has moved past our baseline). Update `baseline` after each successful sync. Keep the human-readable rationale in FORK_WORKFLOW.md in step with this file.

baseline.comment: Last upstream commit fully merged into dev. sync:check compares upstream/dev against this ref. Bump it (and forkTag) after every sync.

_ownedRemoved_2026-09-05.note: packages/opencode/src/session/stream-stalled.ts, packages/opencode/src/session/tool-activity.ts, and packages/opencode/test/session/tool-activity.test.ts were deleted by a90c49880b — confirmed intentional, not a merge regression: a full, reasoned commit message explains that the stream-inactivity watchdog these files implemented only ever fired on false positives (host-paced hybrid loads, foreground subagents, compaction's single big call, cold-load chunks — each already special-cased before this commit finished the trend) and never once caught a genuinely wedged socket, while its false positives were abandoning working turns fleet-wide. Same commit also removed the fork patches this manifest tracked in llm.ts (marker @/local/skein-loading — the SkeinLoading cold-load liveness tick that fed only this watchdog), message-v2.ts (marker StreamStalledError — the error-mapping case for the watchdog's failure type; message-v2.ts no longer diverges from upstream at all and was fully removed from `patched`), and tools.ts (marker "fork: the stream watchdog must not count" — the per-tool-call liveness ticks). llm.ts and tools.ts each still diverge from upstream for unrelated, still-live fork reasons and were re-registered in `patched` with fresh markers (see those entries) rather than dropped — only the watchdog-specific tracking was retired.

_ownedRemoved_2026-08-14.note: packages/opencode/src/util/sync-log.ts was deleted in the origin/dev merge — confirmed intentional, not a merge regression. It was added by 21c1ac9dd6 to give non-Effect call sites (provider.ts, local/placement.ts) a TUI-safe logger after the core/util/log shim was deleted. The dev-side design solved the same problem differently: those helpers now return outcomes (PickOutcome, DiscoveryResult.warnings) and the Effect caller logs (tool/task.ts, provider.ts). That left zero call sites, so the file was removed rather than carried as dead code.

_ownedRemoved_2026-08-13.note: packages/core/src/util/log.ts (the legacy-logger compatibility shim, upstream's own module removed in #31310) was deleted 2026-08-12 — confirmed intentional, not a merge regression: upstream now has its own logger, making the shim genuinely obsolete.

_ownedRemoved_2026-08-12.note: auto-reply.ts, automation-features.ts, pattern-detection.ts (+ its two CLI commands), scheduler.ts, and hook.ts were deliberately deleted 2026-08-07 (commits 88731dfc6f, 0530944759) for being dead/broken code, not lost in a merge. fork:verify was reporting all 7 as regressions because this manifest was never updated at deletion time. Removed here, not re-added.

Appends fork-owned event definitions (loop.updated, side-question.response) to the shared schema manifest. Their schemas live in packages/opencode and cannot be declared in packages/schema, and without this they are absent from the generated Event union so no client can subscribe.

Compaction that itself overflows retries with only the most recent user turn, then falls back to a minimal summary, instead of returning "stop" and stranding the session. Silently lost in the 0d927ba03f merge and only noticed because a fork-only test still asserted it.

Pins LC_ALL=C on git spawns. This code matches git's human-readable output by text (forceRequired), and git localises it — on a non-English machine those checks silently read false.

Disposes each test's instance when the test ends. InstanceStore otherwise holds every instance the suite creates — each with its own :memory: SQLite and slice of the app graph — until the process exits, which measured as the bulk of the suite's memory (provider dir: 3004 -> 2577 MB).

Splits a package specifier from its export subpath. `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock/mantle` is not an installable npm spec — npa cannot parse it, so npm treats it as a local folder and arborist reads <cwd>/@ai-sdk/... Install the base package, resolve the full specifier for the entrypoint.

divergence.note: Ratchet for the failure this fork keeps hitting: a merge silently deleting a fork feature (see the self-healing compaction entry). Any file under `scope` that differs from baseline.upstreamRef and is neither owned/patched nor listed in `accepted` fails fork:verify. `accepted` is the divergence that already existed when the gate was added — classify those as feature or drift over time; new files must be classified immediately. The single remaining accepted entry is packages/core/src/effect/dfdf, which upstream committed by accident — its contents are an editor's "File to save in:" prompt. It is deleted here on purpose; it stays accepted rather than registered because there is no file left to carry a marker. Re-baseline deliberately with `bun run fork:verify --accept-divergence`.
